Meeting Summary (auto):
Skyline is evaluating Redwood for embedding generation + rerank flow. Primary constraints: high throughput (peak ~6k p95 qps), strict 50ms p99 tail for rerank path, and data residency/VPC requirements. Discussed trade-offs between embedding dims (512/768/1536), client-side vector DB sharding, and whether to run Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Action: Redwood to run benchmark sim and provide pricing; Skyline to share workload samples and confirm security questions.

Topics: embeddings dimensionality; vector DB integration and sharding strategy; hybrid retrieval + cross-encoder rerank; hosting models (hosted vs dedicated vs private); KV cache and batching; SOC2/KMS requirements.

Transcript Body:
[00:00:00] Liam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, I'm Liam, I'm the AE, and Maya is our solutions engineer.
[00:00:07] Maya Singh: hi all, hey, excited to dig in. quick note, I might say K V cash instead of KV cache, this transcript's, uh, not perfect.
[00:00:15] Olivia Chen: thanks, yeah Olivia here, i'll try to keep answers focused — we have Marcus and Samir with us from platform and ml.
[00:00:22] Marcus Rivera: morning.
[00:00:24] Samir Patel: hey.
[00:00:26] Liam Carter: Cool. high level - Skyline's goal is to improve search relevance while keeping costs under control and keeping service-level tail latency tight, especially for our checkout help and product search routes. Olivia, can you remind us the qps and dataset sizes?
[00:00:40] Olivia Chen: Sure — baseline qps is 2k average, spikes to 6k on promotions, we expect 10x growth over 12 months. Document corpus for retrieval is ~120 million docs, but we do pruning and tiering so active set is about 15M for realtime retrieval. we were thinking embeddings in the 1536 range but that's partly because our current vendor uses that and we saw slight lift.
[00:01:05] Marcus Rivera: infrastructure wise, we want to keep the vector DB inside our VPC, not SaaS, for PCI/data residency reasons. we are evaluating options to host the index ourselves (Milvus/Pinecone edge) and use a hosted embedding service but open to Dedicated.
[00:01:18] Liam Carter: got it. so a few buckets of conversation today: embedding dims (accuracy vs throughput/cost), where to run encoding vs storage (hosted encoder + self-hosted vector DB vs Redwood Dedicated vs fully private on-prem), and rerank tradeoffs — bi-encoder recall then cross-encoder rerank cost/latency. does that sound right?
[00:01:33] Olivia Chen: yes. and can we cover fallback if the rerank model is slow — like degrade gracefully?
[00:01:38] Maya Singh: absolutely — Redwood supports tiered fallbacks and automatic routing to cheaper/smaller models if latency spikes, and you can set routing policies by route. we'll show concrete routing examples in the benchmarking doc.
[00:01:48] [00:01:50] Samir Patel: quick Q on dims — we saw 1536 give better relevance on fine-grained, especially apparel color/fit queries. But it ballooned our index size and slowed down fanout. what's the typical throughput delta between 512/768/1536 on Redwood hosted inference?
[00:02:04] Maya Singh: rough ballpark — using Redwood hosted generative embeddings, at 512 dims you get about 2–3x higher infer throughput vs 1536 on the same GPU profile because of compute per-row and memory traffic. but there's more to it: storage + network fanout matters. If you plan to do a heavy rerank that runs a cross-encoder per candidate, the embedding dim only affects recall and VDB search speed, not the cross-encoder cost.
[00:02:27] Marcus Rivera: so it's a balance — higher dims improve initial recall and reduce rerank compute maybe, but increase storage and vdb qps cost. we heard about product that does compacting/quantization of embeddings — does Redwood do that or recommend it?
[00:02:39] Maya Singh: Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles and we can host quantized model variants. for embeddings we typically recommend float16 quantization for storage, or post-hoc PQ/HNSW quantization on the vector DB side. but there are precision tradeoffs — we include eval harnesses to compare 512 vs 768 vs 1536 on your exact relevance tests.
[00:02:55] Olivia Chen: interesting. For our SLA we need rerank p99 < 50ms. if we do a hybrid flow — topK 100 from vector DB bi-encoder then cross-encoder rerank top 10 — is that feasible at 6k peak?
[00:03:07] Maya Singh: it's a tight constraint. Let's do some quick math — 6k qps * topK100 means 600k candidate embeddings per second feeding cross-encoder if you naive fanout, which is infeasible. typical pattern: do vector DB topK 100 then cheap lit filter, then cross-encoder only on top 10. So cross-encoder qps becomes 6k*10 = 60k cross-encoder calls per second at peak, which is still significant. Another pattern is approximate rerank with a lightweight MLP or use ANN search that boosts topK quality so you lower topK to 20.
[00:03:38] Samir Patel: 60k cross-encoder qps is expensive. do you have batching or caching options to reduce unit cost?
[00:03:44] Maya Singh: yes — Redwood runtime supports dynamic continuous batching and KV prefix caching (we bucket similar queries). Also, you can cache rerank results for short TTL on common queries; Skyline likely has a heavy tail of repeated queries during promos. We'll run a sim with your qps distribution to estimate batching benefits.
[00:03:58] [00:04:05] Olivia Chen: On hosting — we can't put our index into Redwood hosted for compliance. so two options: (A) Redwood hosted encoder + Skyline self-hosted vector DB in VPC, (B) Redwood Dedicated inside our VPC (private control plane) or (C) full Private on-prem. pros/cons?
[00:04:22] Liam Carter: quick summary: A minimizes infra ops — encoder hosted and we stream embeddings via secure egress; data residency still requires you to control storage. B (Dedicated) gives you reserved capacity and placement in a dedicated tenant with VPC peering options and customer-managed keys — lower latency to your VPC, stronger isolation and SLAs, but higher commit. C is full private install for air-gapped/regulatory heavy customers — most customers choose Dedicated for the best balance.
[00:04:44] Marcus Rivera: If we host vector DB in our VPC, how does Redwood handle secure transfer and key management?
[00:04:49] Maya Singh: we support TLS, client certs, and VPC peering/private link. For keys, Dedicated/Private can integrate with your KMS/HSM — we don't store plaintext keys in our control plane. we can provide SOC2 infosec artifacts; we'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.
[00:05:03] Olivia Chen: great. can you share latency numbers for encoding/embedding per-dim? like p50/p95 for 512/768/1536 on a common GPU?
[00:05:11] Maya Singh: yes — approximate numbers on a common A100 profile: 512 dims: p50 ~6ms, p95 ~12ms; 768: p50 ~9ms p95 ~18ms; 1536: p50 ~18ms p95 ~35ms. Those are single-request numbers; batching increases throughput but p95 can tighten with continuous batching. We'll include exact microbenchmarks in the doc.
[00:05:33] Samir Patel: those p95s are useful. For rerank cross-encoder latency — are you recommending hosting those on Redwood as well? or run them in our infra?
[00:05:41] Maya Singh: either. If you run cross-encoder on Dedicated it can be colocated with the embedding encoder and you get low network overhead. If you run re-rank in your infra, you'll pay the network hop. Many customers use Redwood for encoded embeddings and run cross-encoder in Dedicated or customer VPC for sensitive data and lower latency.
[00:05:57] [00:06:02] Olivia Chen: ok. Another question — sharding the vector DB. With 15M active docs, what kind of shard strategy do you recommend?
[00:06:08] Maya Singh: 15M is mid-size. Common pattern: horizontal sharding by prefix/namespace, keep shards under 5–10M vectors each for HNSW/balanced memory. Also shard by region if you do multi-region read. Our Optimize tool can suggest shard counts given dims and index type.
[00:06:24] Marcus Rivera: What's the expected storage footprint — rough numbers for 1536 float32 vs 512 float16/quantized?
[00:06:29] Maya Singh: 1536 float32 ~ 1536*4 bytes = ~6KB per vector; at 15M that's ~90GB raw but with index overhead it can be 2–3x — expect 200–300GB. With float16 or PQ you drop it dramatically: 512 float16 ~ 512*2 = 1KB per vector so maybe 15–50GB post-index depending. We'll give a sizing table.
[00:06:48] Samir Patel: good. Also, are there examples or customers in retail with similar SLAs?
[00:06:53] Liam Carter: yes, we have references — I'll connect you to a couple of retail customers in EMEA who run Dedicated with similar peak patterns. I'll anonymize details in the reference.
[00:07:01] Olivia Chen: excellent. Security docs — we need SOC2, ISO, the network diagram for VPC peering, and any penetration test summaries.
[00:07:10] Liam Carter: will send our security pack and SOC2 report. Maya will attach the network architecture templates.
[00:07:16] [00:07:20] Marcus Rivera: about cost — can you ballpark monthly cost for Dedicated that can handle 6k peak with headroom?
[00:07:26] Liam Carter: ballpark depends on GPU sku and reserved commit. For an initial estimate — Dedicated with 8x A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale buffer for spikes could be in the mid-five-figures to low-six-figures per month depending on reserved discounts. we'll provide an itemized example comparing hosted inference (pay-as-you-go) vs Dedicated commit.
[00:07:44] Samir Patel: ok. Let's talk about evaluation plan — we'd like a short pilot: 2 weeks of replayed traffic for accuracy & throughput. Is that doable?
[00:07:52] Maya Singh: doable — we commonly do a 2–4 week pilot where we mirror a slice of traffic to Redwood Dedicated or to hosted encoder depending on the option. We'll need sample queries and request shapes to replay.
[00:08:03] Olivia Chen: we'll prepare the replay dataset. Also want to know rollback/fallback: if Dedicated autoscaler fails, do you have automatic fallback to hosted models?
[00:08:13] Maya Singh: yes — Redwood runtime supports fallback policies. You can configure automatic fallback to compatible hosted models or smaller variants to preserve tail SLAs. We also track per-route metrics in the Console so you can set alerts and automatic failovers.
